## Learning Drop

### Key Highlights
- The Confidence Trap of Learning affects at least 30% of learners, preventing them from improving despite studying more than ever.
- The Confidence Trap occurs when individuals think they know enough and stop looking for solutions outside their comfort zone.
- The Confidence Scale method can help overcome the Confidence Trap by identifying discrepancies between confidence and actual skill level.

### Detailed Points
- Dr. Justin at iCanStudy discusses the Confidence Trap of Learning, a phenomenon where learners become overconfident and stop seeking new solutions, ultimately hindering their progress.
- A student named Anna is cited as an example, who spent three years studying mechatronics but failed to improve due to the Confidence Trap.
- The Confidence Trap is defined as a mental shortcut where the brain wants to conserve energy, leading to overconfidence and a lack of awareness about one's shortcomings.
- The Double Burden of Confidence refers to the phenomenon where individuals with low skills not only perform poorly but also lack the ability to recognize their shortcomings.
- The Confidence Scale method is introduced as a solution to overcome the Confidence Trap, involving a 7-step process to identify areas where confidence exceeds actual skill level.
- The steps include:
  * Thinking of an outcome you want to achieve
  * Listing the skills needed to achieve the outcome
  * Rating your confidence level in each skill
  * Evaluating the time and effort spent on developing each skill
  * Identifying discrepancies between confidence and actual skill level
  * Assessing how much you're willing to bet on your confidence
  * Comparing the amount you're willing to bet with the potential losses due to overconfidence
- Dr. Justin encourages readers to try the Confidence Scale method for a goal that's important to them to spot potential Confidence Traps and improve their skills.

## The Rundown AI

### Key Highlights
- Instagram head Adam Mosseri says AI content has made polished posts worthless as proof of authenticity, and the platform must "evolve fast" due to AI.
- DeepSeek hints at next-gen model architecture with a new research paper proposing changes to neural network structure for breakthroughs in model cost and stability.
- OpenAI is reportedly overhauling its audio AI models, laying the groundwork for a voice-first personal device expected in about a year.
- Nebius Token Factory launches Post-training, a platform for fine-tuning AI models like DeepSeek V3 and GPT-OSS 20B & 120B.

### Detailed Points
- Instagram's Adam Mosseri published a year-end essay arguing that AI-generated content has killed the curated aesthetic that made the app famous, suggesting raw, unpolished posts are now the only proof that something is real.
- Mosseri pushed for camera makers to cryptographically sign photos at capture to verify real media instead of just weeding out fakes, and plans to label AI content, surface more context about accounts, and build tools so creators can compete with AI.
- DeepSeek's paper introduces mHC, a technique that stabilizes and improves AI training at a large scale while adding minimal extra computing cost, with tests showing improved benchmark scores over existing methods.
- OpenAI's device ambitions, led by Jony Ive, prioritize voice over screens, with an explicit goal of avoiding smartphone-style addiction, and the company is consolidating multiple teams to improve its audio AI models.
- Nebius Token Factory's Post-training platform allows for fine-tuning of AI models across multi-node GPU clusters with stability up to 131k context.
- The platform offers models deeply adapted to specific domains, tone, structure, and workflows, with one-click deployment and dedicated endpoints.
- Other updates include the release of IQuest-Coder-V1, a new model family that claims to surpass rivals like Claude Sonnet 4.5 and GPT 5.1 on coding benchmarks.
- LMArena posted the 2025 results for top AI models, with Google's Gemini 3 Pro leading text, vision, and search, and Veo 3.1 models topping video rankings.
- Chinese AI startup Kimi reportedly raised $500M in a new Series C round, bringing the company's valuation to $4.3B.
- SoftBank is acquiring DigitalBridge for $4B, adding a data center and digital infrastructure portfolio to the Japanese giant's growing AI bet.

### Key Highlights
- OpenAI is overhauling its audio models and plans to launch an audio-first personal device in about a year, indicating a shift towards an audio-centric future.
- The tech industry is moving towards a future where screens become less prominent and audio takes center stage.
- Robotaxis are expected to be a major transformation this year, with Waymo, Cybercab, and Uber being key players.
- The Large Hadron Collider is being upgraded to improve precision in particle measurements.
- SpaceX's Starlink is reconfiguring its satellite constellation to increase space safety.

- OpenAI has unified its engineering, product, and research teams to improve its audio models, aiming for a more natural sound, handling interruptions, and speaking while users are talking.

- The Large Hadron Collider's upgrade will dominate the tenure of its new director general, Mark Thomson, and will make the LHC more precise in its measurements.
- SpaceX's Starlink is lowering its satellites' altitude to increase space safety and mitigate risks associated with uncoordinated maneuvers and launches.
- The newsletter also covers various topics such as the future of software development, the importance of understanding target users, and the role of culture in driving technological progress.

## The Code by Superhuman

### Key Highlights
- Alibaba's Qwen Image model has become the open-source image king, ranking as the strongest open-source image generator after 10,000+ blind evaluations on AI Arena.
- Hackers are exploiting Google Cloud to bypass email filters and send phishing emails from legitimate Google addresses.
- OpenAI's Sam Altman admits that AI models are presenting real challenges, including the impact on cybersecurity and mental health, and has announced the hiring of a Head of Preparedness to mitigate these risks.

### Detailed Points
- Alibaba's Qwen-Image-2512 model features enhanced human realism and sharper text rendering, and holds its own against closed-source rivals from Google and ByteDance.
- The Qwen family has launched two new TTS models: the voice design model Qwen3-TTS-VD-Flash and the voice cloning model Qwen3-TTS-VC-Flash.
- Google has integrated NotebookLM with Gemini, allowing users to merge notebooks, create images, and build apps.
- Pickle has launched Soul Computer AR glasses that remember your life.
- Researchers have found a prompting trick that boosts LLM creativity by up to 2x with just ~20 extra words.
- LangChain claims that "agent engineering" is the next big discipline, and teams succeeding at this are pioneering a new field that blends product thinking, engineering, and data science.
- HeyGen's CTO argues that the best engineering leaders stay hands-on technically, use that depth to drive strategy, and think of themselves as "directors" of organizational vision.
- Imprint CTO Will Larson argues that even non-AI companies should invest in building internal agent workflows, and shares lessons on skill support, context window compaction, and eval systems.
- A senior engineer reveals how he designs bulletproof APIs, from ditching strict REST to the #1 mistake that causes vulnerabilities.
- Stanford researchers have found a prompting trick that boosts LLM creativity by up to 2x with just ~20 extra words.
- Meta researchers have identified that current AI coders are limited by their need for human-labeled data, and have found that agents using "self-play" to generate and fix their own bugs consistently beat models trained on human examples.

newsletters.summary:
## JournalClub.io Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Researchers from Asia University, Taiwan, proposed a novel approach to android malware detection using an Earthworm Optimization Algorithm (EOA) based cascade LSTM-GRU model.
- The EOA is used to tune the internal hyperparameters of the cascade LSTM-GRU model, which consists of a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network followed by a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) network.
- The proposed model achieved approximately 99% accuracy on a malware dataset, outperforming other models such as standalone LSTM, GRU, RNN, logistic regression, simple feedforward network, and SVM.

### Detailed Points
- The Earthworm Optimization Algorithm (EOA) is a metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of earthworms, which is used to optimize the hyperparameters of the cascade LSTM-GRU model.
- The EOA maintains a population of candidate solutions that diffuse through the search space, combining three signals: the current state, the best-performing solution, and the population mean.
- The authors applied the EOA to optimize the hyperparameters of the cascade LSTM-GRU model, which is designed to detect android malware.
- The cascade model consists of an LSTM network followed by a GRU network, where the LSTM provides temporal stability and the GRU provides discrimination.
- The authors evaluated the performance of the proposed model on a malware dataset and achieved approximately 99% accuracy, outperforming other models.
- The performance gains are attributed to the interaction between feature selection, the cascade design, and global hyperparameter optimization using EOA.
- The EOA is particularly useful for multimodal functions, scheduling problems, continuous parameter search, and any other scenario where the objective surface is discontinuous or difficult to characterize.

Let’s say you’re facing an optimization problem where the search space is continuous, rugged, and poorly behaved. Maybe you’re trying to minimize an objective that has dozens of shallow basins, long plateaus, and only a few narrow global minima. Or maybe the surface is so irregular that even small moves send the search into completely different regions. In this kind of situation, classical gradient-based methods won’t help you, because the function isn’t differentiable everywhere, and the local search gets trapped almost immediately. You need something that can wander, not march.

## Superhuman Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Nvidia has released NitroGen, an open-source foundation model for generalist gaming agents, trained on 40,000 hours of gameplay footage across 1,000+ games.
- SoftBank has completed its $40B investment in OpenAI, giving the company a stake of over 10% in the ChatGPT maker.
- Pickle has launched a wearable device called Pickle 1, which is an AI-powered “soul computer” that captures real-world context via cameras and sensors.

### Detailed Points
- The newsletter discusses the latest developments in AI technology, including the launch of Nvidia's NitroGen, which leverages an overlooked data source: YouTube and Twitch videos with on-screen controller overlays.
- SoftBank's investment in OpenAI is one of the largest private tech deals ever, with part of the capital supporting the Stargate joint venture, a multi-year data center initiative with Oracle.
- Pickle 1 is a 68g aluminum pair of AR glasses designed as a proactive AI companion that organizes personal habits into searchable memory bubbles, running on the memory-driven Pickle OS.
- The newsletter also covers the concept of "invisible walls" in corporate America, where unwritten rules and tacit knowledge hinder the adoption of AI agents, and how solving this issue could unlock true agent automation.
- Additionally, the newsletter provides tips on how to redesign a website with natural language using Google Stitch, and introduces several new AI tools, including SketchTo, Liminary, Unscreen, GoCrazy, and LearnFlux.
